From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — API surface deltas & proposal for compatibility tests

Hi Elaine — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps after our demo and your engineering team's initial questions. I kept this short so your procurement and engineering leads can scan.

TL;DR: Redwood can match the OpenAI-compatible surface for generative + embeddings in most flows; three places to validate in your stack: SDK/transport differences, function-calling parity (named args & JSON schemas), and tokenization/prompt-difference effects on output scoring.

Key differentiation notes (from today):
- Model parity: we run curated open models + tuned variants. Equivalent behavior is achievable by pinning model versions; we'll provide a mapping table for the models we showed.
- API surface: our OpenAI-compatible endpoint supports completions/chat and embeddings. Function-calling is supported but with slightly different schema handling for nested objects — we'll run a parity test.
- SDK swap: client-side changes are typically small (import names, minor call signatures). We can supply a shim and a CodeSandbox sample demonstrating a drop-in switch.
- Security/data residency: Redwood Private gives VPC deployment & KMS integrations; you flagged audit logs/retention — see attached summary.

Proposed 3-step test matrix (we can run this jointly):
1) Sanity parity (low effort): 10 prompts across chat/completions + embeddings. Goal: functional parity; confirm end-to-end requests and outputs.
2) Deterministic prompt diffing (medium): run 50 prompts across the full prompt set, compare tokenization and top-3 outputs. Measure diff rate and where prompts need adjustment.
3) Performance/latency (higher effort): throughput test at typical QPS (50) with realistic sequence lengths (avg 256, p95 1024). Include KV cache enabled vs disabled.

Attachments: api-delta-summary.pdf (short mapping table) and migr-test-plan.md (draft test harness & scripts). I also attached a small benchmark workbook with sample latency numbers.

Ask: Please confirm (a) who on your eng team should be on the tech-run for the tests and (b) whether procurement should get NDA/ordering paperwork now (I can loop in contracts). If you prefer, we can run the sanity parity this week and schedule the full performance run the following week.

Thanks — I’ll wait for a thumbs up and will schedule time with our infra lead (Sergio) to shadow the tests.

—Camila

(See above)

Internal test matrix (priority & owners):
- Sanity parity (Camila/Sergio) — script: migr-test-plan.md, run 10 prompts (chat + embeddings). Expected time: 1 day.
- Schema/function-calling parity (Sergio/Ben) — run our function-calls against their nested invoice schema. Check JSON arg preservation and error surface. Expected time: 2-3 days.
- Tokenization/prompt diffs (Ben) — use token-diff harness, compute per-prompt delta and flag >20% change in token counts or top-1 output shift. Expected time: 2 days.
- Perf baseline (Sergio) — run p95 latencies with KV cache on/off, QPS profile from their usage (they gave sample QPS=50). Expected time: 3 days.

Notes on potential gotchas:
- Embedding vector dimensionality: confirm their current embedding model — if theirs is a different dimension we need a mapping step in the ranker.
- Rate limiting & concurrency: Redwood enforces per-tenant bursts differently than some hyperscalers; we should ensure the harness captures 429 behavior and backoff semantics.
- SDK: building a small compatibility shim is likely a 1-2 day engineering task to normalize call signatures and response envelope for their codebase. Ben, can you estimate?

Files to attach to the run: migr-test-plan.md (script + CLI), redwood-benchmarks-202705.xlsx (sample numbers), api-delta-summary.pdf (mapping table). I've added the HubSpot link to the deal and the draft DocuSign NDA in the related links.

If everyone is aligned I'll coordinate a short kickoff with Mark and procurement.

—Camila
